newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen down on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen down on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday eased after a seven-session rise, despite expectations of further growth, and analysts said the stronger selling after price fixing signalled another fall on Tuesday.
They said lower turnover suggested that current falls represented a downward correction after the market's 9.3-percent growth last week.

"In the context of our growth of more than nine percent last week we can expect a brief correction," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage, who put support for the main WIG-index at 13,000 points.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.5 percent to 13,814.4 and turnover fell 12.7 percent to 94.8 million zlotys ($34.7 million) on both markets. Gainers and losers were even at 32 issues each and 13 stocks were flat.

Some analysts said the market could challenge its July 5, 27-month high in the next week or two, buoyed by foreign institutional buying reflected in last week's higher turnovers over 100 million zlotys ($36.7 million).

Other analysts were not convinced the turnovers reflected such foreign buying which tends to start significant Warsaw uptrends, and said stabilisation or only slow growth could follow the current brief falls.

Biggest loser cement maker Gorazdze, down 4.9 percent in active trade, was hit hardest by profit-taking after recent gains, while top gainer Bank Gdanski, up 5.6 percent in active trade, extended recent gains to an all-time high.

No stocks traded in continuous trade, where mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.7 percent to 88 zlotys ($32.2). On the main market they were flat at 89 zlotys ($32.6) in five-million-zloty ($1.8 million) trade.
